title: rogue legacy
text: Rogue Legacy is a roguelike (duh), bullethell, platformer, where you explore a randomly generated castle collecting gold in order to get better abilities. The biggest draw to this game for me was the fact that everything you earn is passed down to a new heir each time you die. Every heir has their own unique traits, classes, and spells at their disposal. The traits are sometimes helpful like perma-roided which gives you more knockback and drwarfism which makes you tiny and able to reach secret areas of the castle. Other traits however can be silly like colorblindness, nearsightedness, and vertigo, which flips the whole world upside down and reverses the controls. All in all definitely worthwhile if you can get it on sale. I give Rogue Legacy an 8/10

text: the reincarnation mechanic is really interesting! it takes a number of runs of quickly, quickly dying to really get going, but once you start unlocking bonus classes and equipment - permanent bonuses across runs - you can at least survive long enough to get that 175 gold for the next upgrade, since gold doesn't carry over runs. the random characteristic mechanic is pretty cool - every incarnation, you get a choice between three characters with different classes and traits, so you can judge based on your playstyle and what upgrades you have which will be the most successful (or just the most fun!). there's no penalty for a "bad" run, really, except time and frustration. some characters are pretty clearly not gonna last, so you just do your best to get enough gold to improve for when a character that suits you comes along. personally, i love this take on roguelike, still permadeath but almost every death helps out your next run so you don't feel quite so hopeless when you keep. dying. all the time. a lot.

title: rush
text: RUSH is a 3D puzzle game about "pathing":  blocks spawn and automatically move straight ahead, and directional floor tiles must be strategically placed to change the blocks' direction and guide them to the exit.  It starts off easy but gets hard fast, quickly making use of its third dimension and adding other complicating elements like multiple block colors with multiple exits and block-on-block collision.  There's plenty of levels at all difficulties and each one puts their own flavor on the same problem.  Hints are available on most levels for those that want just a little help without getting spoiled; a courteous feature.  Overall a challenging puzzle experience that doesn't overcomplicate things with too many bells and whistles.
